Revoke all active administrator sessions for the currently authenticated admin, implementing the "logout from all devices" functionality. This operation marks all sessions belonging to the admin as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp to the current time, which invalidates all associated refresh tokens and forces re-authentication on every device.

This endpoint serves critical security purposes including responding to suspected account compromise, handling lost or stolen devices that were logged in, enforcing security policy after administrative password changes, and providing peace of mind when an admin is uncertain about their session state across multiple devices.

The operation queries the todo_list_admin_sessions table for all sessions belonging to the authenticated admin (identified by the admin ID from the JWT token) that have null expired_at values, indicating they are currently active. All matching sessions are updated to set expired_at to the current timestamp, effectively terminating them simultaneously.

Upon successful execution, all of the admin's refresh tokens become invalid. Any devices or browsers that had active admin sessions will be unable to refresh their access tokens when they expire. Users on those devices will be required to authenticate again with their email and password to restore access to administrative functions.

The operation returns an empty success response (204 No Content) upon successful completion. The system may send email notification to the admin's registered email address confirming the security action, including the timestamp and originating IP address of the revocation request.

This operation is distinct from single-session revocation and represents the most aggressive session management action available to administrators. It should be used when comprehensive session termination is required for security purposes.

Clients should never send pre-hashed passwords.

Current password for identity verification when changing password.

This field is required when the password field is provided. The system verifies the current password matches the stored hash before allowing password changes. This security measure prevents unauthorized password modifications if someone gains temporary access to an authenticated session.

If the current password verification fails, the operation is rejected with an authentication error. This ensures users must prove knowledge of the existing password before establishing a new one.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying authenticated user's account information.

This schema defines the mutable fields users can update on their own accounts. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates where users can change just email, just password, or both in a single operation. If no fields are provided, the operation succeeds without modifications.

Email updates: When email is provided, it must pass format validation and uniqueness checks. The system normalizes email to lowercase before storage. If validation fails, specific error messages indicate the issue (invalid format, already registered, etc.).

Password updates: When password is provided, current_password becomes required for identity verification. The new password must meet complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters, mixed case, digits, special characters). Upon successful password change, all refresh tokens except the current session are invalidated, forcing re-authentication on other devices for security.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed whenever any modification occurs, providing audit trail capability. The id and created_at fields are immutable and cannot be modified through this operation.

Security considerations: This DTO never includes password_hash or any internal authentication fields. The password field accepts plain text in the request (transmitted over HTTPS), which the backend hashes before storage. Users can only update their own account identified by the JWT token - there is no way to specify a different user ID.

current_password.description:
The user's current password for identity verification.

This field is required to authenticate the password change request and prevent unauthorized password modifications. The provided password must exactly match the current password_hash stored in the todo_list_users table.

The system validates this password using the same secure hashing algorithm used during authentication. If the current password does not match, the operation fails with an authentication error to protect against unauthorized access.

new_password.description:
The new password to set for the user account.

This password must meet all password complexity and security requirements defined in the system specification. The password must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character from the allowed set.

The system validates the new password against strength requirements before accepting it. Upon successful validation, the password is securely hashed using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt or argon2) with appropriate computational cost factors before being stored in the password_hash field of the todo_list_users table.

The new password must be different from the current password to ensure meaningful security updates.

ITodoListUser.IChangePassword.description:
Request body for changing a user's password.

This DTO encapsulates the information required to securely update a user's password. It enforces a two-step verification process by requiring both the current password (for identity verification) and the new password (for the update).

The structure implements security best practices by validating the user's identity through current password verification before allowing credential changes. This prevents unauthorized password modifications if a user's active session is compromised.

All password fields in this request are transmitted as plain text over secure HTTPS connections and are immediately hashed upon receipt by the backend. The backend never stores plain text passwords and applies industry-standard hashing algorithms before any database operations.

This DTO is used exclusively in the password change operation and does not include any user identity fields (like user_id) since the authenticated user context is derived from the JWT token.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password change operation completed successfully.

A value of true confirms that the password was successfully updated in the todo_list_users table and all existing sessions (except the current one) were invalidated. A value of false would indicate a failure, though in practice the API returns error responses rather than success:false for failed operations.

This field provides explicit confirmation of the operation outcome for client-side processing and user feedback.

message.description:
Human-readable confirmation message describing the password change outcome.

Typically contains a success message such as "Password changed successfully. You have been logged out of all other devices." This message informs the user that their password update was successful and that security measures (session revocation) have been applied.

The message provides actionable information to help users understand the security implications of the password change, particularly that they will need to re-authenticate on other devices due to session invalidation.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordChanged.description:
Response body confirming successful password change.

This DTO provides confirmation that the password update operation completed successfully and describes the security measures that were automatically applied. The response structure is designed to inform users about both the immediate outcome (password changed) and the security side effects (session revocation).

When a password is successfully changed, the backend performs several operations atomically: updates the password_hash field in todo_list_users, invalidates all refresh tokens except the current session by updating expired_at in todo_list_user_sessions, and commits the transaction. This response confirms all these operations completed successfully.

The response intentionally does not include sensitive information such as the new password hash or session identifiers. It provides only the confirmation status and a user-friendly message suitable for display in the application UI.

This DTO is returned exclusively from the password change operation after successful validation of the current password and acceptance of the new password according to security requirements.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user session record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the session in the database and is used in API operations to reference specific sessions when retrieving details or terminating sessions.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the user who owns this session.

Links this session to the authenticated user account in the todo_list_users table. This relationship enables the system to enforce data isolation by ensuring users can only access their own sessions.

ip.description:
IP address from which the session was established.

Captures the client's IP address at the time of authentication for security monitoring and audit trail purposes. This field helps users identify sessions from unfamiliar locations that might indicate unauthorized access.

Used for security monitoring, audit trails, and identifying suspicious authentication patterns as documented in the Prisma schema.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the application page where the session was established.

Records the full URL of the application entry point when the user authenticated. This provides context about how the session was initiated and helps users understand the connection context for security purposes.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the page that led to the authentication.

Captures the HTTP referrer header value at the time of session creation, showing which page or external source directed the user to authenticate. This helps track session origin and user navigation patterns for security analysis.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created.

Records the exact date and time when the user successfully authenticated and the session was established. This information helps users identify when they logged in from different devices and supports security auditing by showing session creation chronology.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was terminated or expired.

Null for active sessions that are currently valid. Set to the termination timestamp when a session ends through logout, token expiration, or security-related revocation. This field distinguishes between active and inactive sessions and maintains an audit trail of when sessions were ended.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
User authentication session entity representing JWT refresh token lifecycle and connection context.

This entity tracks individual user authentication sessions in the todo_list_user_sessions table. Each session corresponds to a JWT refresh token issued during login and maintains metadata about the authentication event including connection origin, timing, and status.

Sessions enable users to maintain authenticated access across multiple devices and browsers simultaneously. The system supports viewing all active sessions, retrieving specific session details, and terminating individual sessions for security management.

The entity captures connection context through IP address, application URL (href), and referrer to provide visibility into where sessions originated. This information supports security monitoring by helping users identify unfamiliar sessions that might indicate unauthorized access.

Session lifecycle is managed through created_at and expired_at timestamps. Active sessions have null expired_at values, while terminated sessions show when they were ended. Session termination occurs through explicit logout, token expiration, or security-related revocation such as logout from all devices.

The relationship to todo_list_users enforces strict data isolation - users can only access and manage their own sessions. This prevents cross-user session visibility and ensures proper authorization boundaries.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrator account.

Primary key used to identify the admin across the system and in session relationships. This UUID is generated upon admin account creation and remains immutable throughout the account lifecycle.

Used as the foreign key reference in todo_list_admin_sessions table to link authentication sessions to specific administrator accounts.

email.description:
Administrator's email address used for authentication and identification.

Must be unique across all admin accounts to ensure each email corresponds to exactly one administrator. Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for consistency and stored in the Prisma schema with unique constraint enforcement.

Serves as the primary credential for admin login and is displayed in admin profile views and account management interfaces.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

Records the exact date and time the admin account was registered in the system. Used for account lifecycle tracking, administrative auditing purposes, and displaying account age in admin management interfaces.

Stored in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z') and automatically set during account creation. This value is immutable and never changes after initial creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last modification to the administrator account.

Automatically updated whenever account credentials or information changes, such as password modifications or email updates. Provides audit trail for account security and helps track when credentials were last changed.

Stored in ISO 8601 format and reflects the most recent update operation. Particularly useful for security monitoring to identify when password changes occurred.

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:
Lightweight administrator account summary for profile display and references.

Provides essential admin identification and metadata for displaying administrator account information in profile views, list contexts, and embedded references. This summary variant includes core identification fields plus account lifecycle timestamps without exposing sensitive credential information.

Used as the response type for admin profile retrieval operations and after successful account updates. Excludes password_hash and other sensitive security fields that should never be transmitted in API responses.

The ISummary variant balances completeness with security, providing sufficient information for account management interfaces while maintaining proper security boundaries by omitting authentication secrets.

current_password.description:
Current password for identity verification before allowing account changes.

Required to verify the admin's identity and prevent unauthorized password changes even if a session token is compromised. The provided password is validated against the stored password_hash in the todo_list_admins table using secure comparison of bcrypt or argon2 hashes.

This verification step is mandatory for all password change operations as defined in the authentication requirements. If verification fails, the operation returns an error 'Current password is incorrect' without revealing whether the account exists.

Must meet the same minimum length requirement of 8 characters as all passwords in the system, though it should match whatever password was previously set regardless of historical validation rules.

new_password.description:
New password to set for the administrator account with strong security requirements.

Must meet comprehensive password strength requirements for administrative accounts: minimum 8 characters including at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special character. These requirements match the password validation rules defined in the authentication security specifications.

The password is securely hashed using bcrypt or argon2 algorithms before storage in the password_hash field of todo_list_admins table. The plaintext password is never stored or logged.

Successful password change triggers automatic session invalidation: all existing admin sessions except the current one are revoked by invalidating their refresh tokens, forcing re-authentication on other devices. The admin also receives email notification confirming the password change with timestamp and IP address for security awareness and fraud detection.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating administrator account credentials through secure password change.

Used when authenticated administrators update their own account passwords following the self-service account management pattern. Implements the secure password change flow where admins can modify their credentials independently without requiring another administrator's assistance.

Security enforcement is multi-layered: the admin_id is extracted from JWT token authentication context rather than request body, ensuring admins can only modify their own accounts. Current password verification is mandatory before applying changes, preventing unauthorized modifications even with compromised session tokens.

Follows the same password change security flow as regular users but applies to administrative accounts. Validation provides specific feedback about which password strength requirements are not met when new_password fails validation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrator account.

Primary key that uniquely identifies this admin across the system. Used for session tracking, audit trails, and all administrative operation references.

email.description:
Administrator's email address used for authentication and identification.

Must be unique across all admin accounts. Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for consistency and to enable case-insensitive authentication. This email serves as the primary login credential and identification mechanism for administrative access.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

Automatically set during admin account creation and never modified thereafter. Used for account lifecycle tracking, administrative auditing purposes, and determining account age for security policies.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last modification to the administrator account.

Updated automatically when account credentials or information changes, such as password updates or email modifications. Provides temporal context for account changes and supports audit trail requirements.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Administrator account entity with elevated system privileges.

Represents system administrators who have elevated permissions for user management, system monitoring, and administrative operations. Admins authenticate using JWT-based mechanisms and receive tokens with admin role and expanded permissions.

Admins can perform operations beyond regular user capabilities including viewing all user accounts, managing user status, accessing system-wide statistics, and supporting users. All administrative actions are logged for accountability and security auditing.

Security note: The password_hash field is excluded from all response DTOs for security. Admin sessions are managed through the related ITodoListAdminSession entity for JWT refresh token tracking and connection context.

current_password.description:
Administrator's current password for verification.

Required to verify that the password change request is made by the legitimate account owner. Must match the existing password_hash after hashing. This security measure prevents unauthorized password changes even if someone gains access to an authenticated session.

new_password.description:
New password to set for the administrator account.

Must meet strong password requirements enforced during account creation. Will be securely hashed using industry-standard algorithms (bcrypt or argon2) before storage. The password should be sufficiently complex to protect administrative access to the system.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdatePassword.description:
Request body for administrator password update operation.

Contains both the current password for verification and the new password to be set. This structure enforces a secure password change flow where admins must prove ownership of the account before modifying credentials.

Successful password updates will invalidate all existing admin sessions except the current one, requiring re-authentication on all other devices. This security measure prevents unauthorized access if the password was changed due to suspected compromise.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrator session.

Primary key that uniquely identifies this admin session across the system. Used to reference specific sessions for inspection, revocation, or security auditing purposes.

todo_list_admin_id.description:
Administrator who owns this session.

Foreign key reference to todo_list_admins.id indicating which admin account this session belongs to. Each session is associated with exactly one administrator account for proper access control and session isolation.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin session was established.

Critical for security monitoring and detecting unauthorized administrative access attempts. Used in audit trails and for identifying suspicious authentication patterns that may indicate compromised credentials.

href.description:
Connection URL where the admin authentication request originated.

Provides context about the admin interface entry point for this session. Helps track which administrative interface was used to establish the session and supports troubleshooting of authentication flows.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the source that led to the admin authentication request.

Helps track administrative access patterns and entry points. Provides context about how the admin reached the authentication page, which is useful for security analysis and understanding admin navigation patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session was created through administrator login.

Marks the beginning of this authenticated administrative session. Used for calculating session age, enforcing session timeouts, and providing temporal context in audit logs.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session ended or will end.

Null for currently active sessions. Set when admin logs out, token expires, or session is revoked due to password change or security actions. Provides clear indication of session lifecycle status and supports session cleanup operations.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Administrator authentication session for JWT refresh token management.

Tracks active administrator sessions with JWT-based authentication patterns. Admin sessions store refresh token information and connection context to enable secure session management and revocation capabilities.

Administrative sessions grant elevated permissions through the admin role encoded in JWT tokens. Session tracking enables security features like logout, password reset requiring re-authentication, and 'logout from all devices' functionality.

Connection context (IP, URL, referrer) is recorded for each admin session to support security auditing and investigation of administrative actions. This provides accountability and helps detect unauthorized access attempts to administrative functions. Multiple concurrent admin sessions are supported to allow administrators to access the system from different devices simultaneously.

revoked_count.description:
Number of active admin sessions that were successfully revoked. This count represents all sessions belonging to the authenticated administrator that were marked as expired during the bulk revocation operation.

The count includes sessions from all devices and browsers where the admin was logged in. A count of zero indicates the admin had no active sessions at the time of revocation, which is unusual but possible if all sessions had already expired naturally or were previously revoked individually.

This metric is important for security auditing and helps administrators verify the scope of the logout action.

revoked_at.description:
Timestamp when the bulk session revocation was executed. This represents the exact moment when all admin sessions were marked as expired by setting their expired_at values.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone. This timestamp is critical for security audit trails and correlating session termination with potential security incidents or administrative actions.

The same timestamp value is used as the expired_at value for all revoked sessions, providing consistent temporal reference for the bulk operation.

notification_sent.description:
Indicates whether the security notification email was successfully sent to the administrator's registered email address.

A value of true confirms that the admin received confirmation of the session revocation action, including details about the timestamp and originating IP address. This notification serves as both confirmation of intentional actions and early warning of potential unauthorized access.

A value of false indicates email delivery failure, which should prompt administrators to verify their email settings or check spam filters for the security notification.

ITodoListAdminSessionRevocationSummary.description:
Summary response for bulk admin session revocation operation. This schema provides comprehensive feedback about the 'logout from all devices' security action, including metrics about how many sessions were terminated and confirmation of security notifications.

This response type is returned when an administrator invokes the session revocation endpoint to terminate all their active sessions simultaneously. The operation is typically performed for security purposes such as responding to suspected account compromise, handling lost devices, or enforcing re-authentication after password changes.

The schema includes the count of revoked sessions to help administrators understand the scope of the action, the precise timestamp of revocation for audit trail purposes, and confirmation that security notifications were sent to alert the admin about this significant account activity.

Administrators can use this information to verify that the security action completed as expected and that appropriate notifications were delivered.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Determines which subset of results to return based on the limit parameter.

For example, with limit=10, page=1 returns items 1-10, page=2 returns items 11-20, and so forth. This zero-indexed approach provides intuitive navigation through large todo lists.

Defaults to 1 if not specified, showing the first page of results.

limit.description:
Number of todo items to return per page. Controls the page size for pagination results.

Accepts values between 1 and 100 to balance between granular control and performance. Smaller limits provide more frequent pagination but require more requests for large lists. Larger limits reduce total requests but may impact response time and client rendering performance.

Defaults to a reasonable value (typically 20-50) if not specified, optimized for common list display scenarios.

search.description:
Search term for partial matching against todo item titles. Performs case-insensitive substring search to find todos whose titles contain the search term.

For example, searching 'meeting' would match todos titled 'Team Meeting', 'Prepare meeting notes', and 'Meeting with client'. The search is designed for natural, user-friendly queries without requiring exact matches or special syntax.

When omitted or empty, no title filtering is applied and all todos matching other criteria are returned. Combined with status filtering and sorting options for comprehensive search capabilities.

status.description:
Filter todos by completion status. Accepts one of three values to control which todos are returned based on their completion state.

'completed' - Returns only todos where completed is true, showing finished tasks. Useful for reviewing accomplished items or generating completion reports.

'incomplete' - Returns only todos where completed is false, showing pending tasks. This is the most common filter for active task management, displaying what still needs to be done.

null or omitted - Returns all todos regardless of completion status, providing a complete view of all tasks. This default behavior ensures users see their entire task list unless they explicitly filter.

The filter applies after search term matching and before sorting and pagination, ensuring accurate result sets.

oneOf.description:
Field to use for sorting the todo list results. Determines the primary ordering criterion before pagination is applied.

'created_at' - Sort by creation timestamp. Useful for viewing tasks in chronological order of entry, helping users find recently added items or review task history.

'updated_at' - Sort by last modification timestamp. Helps identify recently modified todos, tracking which items have had recent activity or changes.

'completed' - Sort by completion status. Groups completed and incomplete todos together, with the specific order determined by the sort_order parameter. Useful for separating finished from pending tasks.

Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified, providing chronological organization as the standard view. Combined with sort_order to achieve precise result ordering.

oneOf.description:

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating the authenticated user's todo list. This schema defines the comprehensive query interface for todo list retrieval operations.

Supports flexible search capabilities through partial title matching, precise filtering by completion status, and customizable sorting by creation date, update date, or completion status. Pagination controls allow efficient handling of large task lists with configurable page sizes.

All parameters are optional, with sensible defaults applied when not specified. The default behavior returns all todos sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) with standard pagination settings.

The search and filtering operations are applied before sorting and pagination to ensure accurate result sets. Soft-deleted todos (where deleted_at is not null) are automatically excluded from all queries to show only active tasks.

This request schema enables rich user experiences including search-as-you-type functionality, status-based task organization, and flexible list views tailored to different task management workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo item.

UUID that uniquely identifies this task in the system. Used for referencing the todo in update and delete operations.

title.description:
Title or description of the todo task.

The main content describing what needs to be done. Provides essential information for task identification in list views.

completed.description:
Completion status of the todo item.

Indicates whether the task is completed (true) or pending (false). Essential for filtering and displaying task status in list views.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo was created.

Provides creation time information for sorting and displaying todos chronologically. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a todo item for list views.

Optimized version of the todo entity containing only essential fields needed for displaying todos in list contexts. Excludes user_id for cleaner presentation since the user context is implied in personal todo lists.

Excludes completed_at and updated_at timestamps to reduce payload size while maintaining core functionality for task lists. This representation is ideal for paginated todo list responses where complete detail is not required.

Used in list operations and anywhere a compact todo representation is needed.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo item.

This UUID is automatically generated by the system when the todo is created and serves as the primary key for the todo_list_todos table. It uniquely identifies each task in the user's todo list.

Used for referencing specific todos in update and delete operations.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Unique identifier of the user who owns this todo item.

This field establishes the ownership relationship between the todo and its creator. It references the id field in the todo_list_users table and is used for authorization checks to ensure users can only access and modify their own todos.

Automatically populated from the authenticated user's JWT token during todo creation. This foreign key field maintains referential integrity with the todo_list_users table.

title.description:
Title or description of the todo task.

This is the main content of the todo item, describing what task needs to be completed. It should be clear and concise to help users understand what action is required.

Must be a non-empty string with a maximum length of 500 characters as defined in the Prisma schema. Users can update this field to modify task details or correct information.

completed.description:
Completion status of the todo item.

Indicates whether the task has been completed (true) or is still pending (false). This field allows users to track their progress and filter between active and completed tasks.

When set to true, the system automatically updates the completed_at timestamp. When set to false, the completed_at timestamp is cleared.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed.

Automatically set by the system when the completed field transitions from false to true. Provides historical tracking of when tasks were finished, useful for productivity analysis and reporting.

Null when the todo is not completed or has been unmarked as complete. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was created.

Automatically set by the system during todo creation and cannot be modified. Provides audit trail and allows sorting todos by creation time.

Uses ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z).

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was last updated.

Automatically updated by the system whenever the todo is modified (title changed, completion status toggled, etc.). Helps track recent changes and activity.

Uses ISO 8601 date-time format and is always set to the current time when any update operation occurs.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for audit trail support.

Null for active todos that have not been deleted. Set to the current timestamp when a user deletes the todo item, marking it as deleted while preserving the record in the database for historical and audit purposes.

Soft deletion allows the system to maintain complete data history while excluding deleted todos from normal query results. This supports potential data recovery scenarios and provides administrators with visibility into deleted content for compliance and auditing requirements.

Uses ISO 8601 date-time format. Once set, the todo is considered deleted and will not appear in the user's active todo list, though the record remains in the todo_list_todos table.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Complete todo item entity representing a user's task.

Represents individual todo items in the user's task list, tracking both the task details and completion status. Each todo is owned by a specific user through the todo_list_user_id foreign key and includes metadata for creation and update timestamps.

Todos support basic task management features including title updates and completion tracking. The completed_at timestamp provides historical data about when tasks were finished. The deleted_at timestamp enables soft deletion for audit trail support.

Used in detailed todo retrieval responses, update operation responses, and as the full representation of todo items across the API.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Todo item creation request body for adding new tasks to the user's todo list.

This DTO defines the data required to create a new todo item. It includes only the business fields that users provide when adding a task - specifically the title describing what needs to be done.

System-managed fields are automatically handled by the backend and excluded from this request body. The user_id is extracted from the JWT authentication token to ensure users can only create todos for themselves. The id is auto-generated using UUID. Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are automatically set by the system. The completed status defaults to false for new todos. The completed_at and deleted_at fields are initially null.

This DTO enforces security by preventing users from specifying user_id or any system-managed fields in the request, ensuring proper data isolation and automatic timestamp management.

title.description:
Title or description of the task to be completed.

This is the user-provided description of what needs to be done. It must be a non-empty string (minimum 1 character) with a maximum length of 500 characters as defined in the Prisma schema. The title should be descriptive enough for the user to understand the task requirements.

Updated title or description of the todo task.

Optional field allowing users to modify the task description. When provided, must be a non-empty string. The new title replaces the existing one completely.

If omitted, the todo's title remains unchanged.

completed.description:
Updated completion status of the todo item.

Optional field allowing users to mark tasks as complete (true) or incomplete (false). When set to true, the system automatically sets the completed_at timestamp. When set to false, the completed_at timestamp is cleared.

If omitted, the completion status remains unchanged.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing todo item.

Contains optional fields for modifying a todo's title and completion status. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates where only specified fields are changed.

The system automatically updates the updated_at timestamp when any field is modified. When the completed field is set to true, the completed_at timestamp is automatically populated. When set to false, completed_at is cleared.

Ownership verification ensures only the todo's owner can perform updates.
